tools.name: project.create
tools.description: Create a new film project (§11.1)

tools.name: project.list_for_owner
tools.description: List every project a user owns, most recently updated first

tools.name: project.update
tools.description: Rename a project or change its description

tools.name: project.delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a project and everything in it (tracks, scenes, assets, render history). Cannot be undone.

tools.name: project.get_state
tools.description: Fetch a project's full current state: project, tracks, scenes, timeline items, placeholders, scenarios

tools.name: project.get_summary
tools.description: Fetch a compact project summary (project settings, tracks, scene list) — prefer this over project.get_state for normal conversation context (§16)

tools.name: project.export
tools.description: Export a project's full structure (settings, tracks, scenes, timeline, placeholders, transitions, current prompts) as a portable JSON document, suitable for project.import

tools.name: project.import
tools.description: Create a brand-new project from a project.export JSON document. Only relinks media whose asset id still exists and is owned by ownerId; anything else comes in unresolved.

tools.name: track.create
tools.description: Create a video or audio track on a project (§11.4)

tools.name: track.update
tools.description: Rename, mute, lock, or set the volume (0-1) of a track

tools.name: track.delete
tools.description: Delete a track

tools.name: track.reorder
tools.description: Move a track to a new position among the project's tracks — video and audio tracks share one ordering, so a track can move in between tracks of either type

tools.name: scene.create
tools.description: Create a storytelling scene on a project — distinct from a timeline clip (§7.2, §11.3)

tools.name: scene.update
tools.description: Update a scene's title, summary, narrative purpose, planned duration, or location (its shots inherit the location unless they override it)

tools.name: scene.reorder
tools.description: Move a scene to a new position among the project's scenes

tools.name: scene.delete
tools.description: Delete a scene

tools.name: timeline.add_placeholder
tools.description: Add a video/audio placeholder clip to a track, ready for a generation prompt (§7.5, §11.5)

tools.name: timeline.move_item
tools.description: Move a timeline item to a new start time, and optionally to a different track (must be the same track type — video to video, audio to audio — and the item must not be a transition or have one attached)

tools.name: timeline.duplicate_item
tools.description: Duplicate a timeline clip (media or placeholder, not a transition), by default onto the same track immediately after itself, pushing whatever else is later on that track to the right to make room (only fails if the target spot would land inside another clip that starts before it). Pass trackId to du

tools.name: timeline.trim_item
tools.description: Trim a timeline item's start, duration, or source in/out points

tools.name: timeline.set_speed
tools.description: Change a clip's playback speed (0.2 = 5x slower, 1 = normal, 1.8 = 1.8x faster). Recomputes the clip's timeline duration for the new speed and ripples everything later on the same track to stay contiguous — the source range consumed is unchanged, only how long it takes to play.

tools.name: timeline.set_volume
tools.description: Set a clip's own audio gain (0 = silent, 1 = full). Multiplies with its track's volume — both apply together — so a clip can be ducked or muted independent of the rest of its track.

tools.name: timeline.set_transform
tools.description: Place a clip on a video track as a layer: its position, size and opacity in the frame. Video tracks stack by order (higher order is drawn on top), and anything outside a scaled-down or transparent clip shows the tracks beneath — so a logo, watermark or picture-in-picture is an image/GIF/video placeh

tools.name: timeline.split_item
tools.description: Split a timeline item into two at an absolute timeline position

tools.name: timeline.delete_item
tools.description: Delete a timeline item (and its placeholder, if any)

tools.name: timeline.close_gap
tools.description: Ripple a timeline item (and everything after it on the same track) earlier to eat the empty space immediately before it. Fails if there is no gap before the item.

tools.name: timeline.batch
tools.description: Apply SEVERAL timeline edits in ONE call — one version check, one result, one undo step, all-or-nothing (if any op fails nothing is applied and the error names the failing op). ALWAYS prefer this over repeated single-edit calls whenever you have two or more timeline edits to make (e.g. trimming five

tools.name: timeline.close_gaps
tools.description: Close the empty gaps between SEVERAL clips at once (a ripple: each clip after the first is pulled left against its predecessor, and everything later on the track moves with it, so clips after the span keep their spacing). Select the clips with exactly one of itemIds (every gap inside the span from t

tools.name: timeline.add_transition
tools.description: Add a transition (§4.1: crossfade, smooth_blend, fade_from_black, or fade_to_black — a hard cut needs no call at all, it's just the default). crossfade and smooth_blend require fromItemId and toItemId to be two contiguous, back-to-back clips on the same track, and shift toItemId durationMs earlier s

tools.name: timeline.add_transitions
tools.description: Add the SAME transition to several clips in ONE call (and one undo step) — prefer this over repeated timeline.add_transition when joining a run of clips. Select the clips with exactly one of itemIds, trackId (every clip on a track) or all:true (every clip on every track; trackType limits to video/au

tools.name: timeline.remove_transitions
tools.description: Remove transitions from several clips in ONE call (and one undo step): every transition whose clip(s) are all selected (itemIds, trackId or all:true, like timeline.add_transitions) — a crossfade/smooth_blend needs both its clips selected, a fade just its own clip. Crossfaded clips are shifted back t

tools.name: timeline.remove_transition
tools.description: Remove a transition. For a crossfade or smooth_blend this also shifts the incoming clip back to its pre-transition position.

tools.name: timeline.update_transition_duration
tools.description: Change how long an existing fade, crossfade or smooth_blend lasts, in ms. For a crossfade or smooth_blend this re-shifts the incoming clip to keep it anchored to the outgoing clip's end.

tools.name: asset.replace_placeholder
tools.description: Point a placeholder at a real uploaded/generated asset (§11.7, §18.2). Preserves the placeholder and its prompt for provenance; sets its status to 'generated'.

tools.name: asset.get
tools.description: Fetch one asset's metadata (type, source, mime type, duration/dimensions if known) plus a downloadUrl for its file: a plain HTTP GET, no auth header needed, valid 24h (call again for a fresh one)

tools.name: asset.list
tools.description: List every asset uploaded/generated for a project (§11.7)

tools.name: scenario.create
tools.description: Stage a concept + treatment + scene list before materializing it onto the timeline (§9, §11.2). Does not touch tracks/scenes/timeline — call scenario.apply_to_timeline next.

tools.name: scenario.get
tools.description: Fetch a staged scenario's concept, treatment, and scene list

tools.name: scenario.update
tools.description: Revise a staged scenario's concept, treatment, and/or scene list before applying it — e.g. after the user asks for a pacing or tone change. Only the fields provided are changed.

tools.name: scenario.delete
tools.description: Delete a staged scenario draft (does not affect anything already applied to the timeline)

tools.name: scenario.apply_to_timeline
tools.description: The high-level film-building tool (§34): materializes a staged scenario into real tracks, scenes, placeholders, and timeline items in one atomic, undoable step. Creates a video track with one placeholder per scene; optionally a Music track with one placeholder spanning the whole scenario, an SFX tra

tools.name: storyline.get
tools.description: Fetch the Scenario Maker draft storyline for a project: the premise (and how many reference images it has), the scenes the user has accepted so far (path), and the current batch of suggested next scenes (candidates).

tools.name: storyline.set_premise
tools.description: Set the Scenario Maker premise (initial scene or short scenario), optionally with up to 3 reference images (base64) that define the look and setting. Resets the accepted path and candidates. Needs a premise or at least one image.

tools.name: storyline.set_candidates
tools.description: Replace the current batch of suggested next scenes with distinct options you propose, so the user can pick one. Each option should follow from the premise and every scene already in the path.

tools.name: storyline.pick
tools.description: Accept one of the current candidates as the next scene in the storyline, optionally with edits. Clears the candidates — suggest new ones afterwards.

tools.name: storyline.update_scene
tools.description: Edit a scene already accepted into the storyline path

tools.name: storyline.rewind
tools.description: Rewind the storyline: keep only the first `keep` accepted scenes (0 clears the path) and discard the rest and the current candidates, so a different choice can be made at that point.

tools.name: storyline.apply
tools.description: Turn the accepted storyline path into real scenes, placeholders, prompts and timeline items in one undoable step (stages it as a scenario and applies it), then clears the draft path. With draftShots (default true) each scene is first broken into a shot list like shot.draft (metered in credits unless

tools.name: prompt.attach
tools.description: Attach a structured prompt document to a scene slot (visual/sound/music/voice) or a placeholder directly (§8, §11.6)

tools.name: prompt.update
tools.description: Revise a prompt — creates a new revision rather than overwriting the old one (§17)

tools.name: prompt.get
tools.description: Fetch one prompt document by id

tools.name: prompt.list_for_scene
tools.description: List every prompt ever attached to a scene, across all slots and revisions

tools.name: prompt.list_revisions
tools.description: Get the full revision history (oldest first) for a prompt's slot, given any promptId in that lineage (§17)

tools.name: project.undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent operation applied to a project (§14)

tools.name: render.preview
tools.description: Start a fast, half-resolution preview export of the project's current timeline to MP4 (§11.8). Takes the same aspect/fit as render.final so the framing can be checked cheaply. Costs 1 credit, charged to the project owner; fails with INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS if they can't cover it.

tools.name: render.final
tools.description: Start a full-resolution final export of the project's current timeline to MP4 (§11.8). Costs 5 credits at 1080p (the default), 10 at 2k (2560x1440) or 15 at 4k, charged to the project owner; fails with INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS if they can't cover it. The resolution is the short side for portrait/square

tools.name: credits.get_balance
tools.description: Get the credit balance of the project's owner, and what a render costs, in milli-credits (1000 = 1 credit). Check this before starting a render if the balance may be low.

tools.name: credits.list_history
tools.description: List the project owner's credit history, newest first: purchases, assistant usage, renders and AI generations, each with its signed amount in milli-credits (1000 = 1 credit; negative = spent), balance after, detail (model, resolution, tokens…) and the project it was for. Also returns net spend per c

tools.name: render.status
tools.description: Check the status/progress of a render job

tools.name: render.get_result
tools.description: Get a completed render job's result: the output assetId and a downloadUrl for the rendered file — a plain HTTP GET, no auth header needed, valid 24h (call again for a fresh one)

tools.name: render.list_for_project
tools.description: List every render job ever started for a project, most recent first

tools.name: render.delete
tools.description: Remove a render job from the project's export list. If it finished, its output file is deleted too. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: asset.upload
tools.description: Upload a video, audio or image file into a project's media library. Send the file bytes as base64 (max 50 MB; larger files must be uploaded in the browser). Returns the new assetId.

tools.name: asset.capture_frame
tools.description: Grab one frame of a video asset (e.g. a take) as a new PNG image asset. timeMs is the position in the video itself, not on the timeline. Save the result with shot.add_still, location.add_reference or character.add_reference.

tools.name: prompt.draft
tools.description: Draft three alternative generation prompts for a scene's asset (metered in credits unless the owner uses their own Anthropic key). Returns the variants; attach one to a scene with prompt.attach.

tools.name: shot.draft
tools.description: Draft a shot list for one scene — shot sizes, angles, movement, lens, f-stop, focus — from the scene, the film look and the cast (metered in credits unless the owner uses their own Anthropic key). Returns drafts only; create the ones you want with shot.create.

tools.name: storyline.suggest
tools.description: Suggest next scenes for the project's storyline from its premise (metered in credits unless the owner uses their own Anthropic key). Requires storyline.set_premise first. The suggestions become candidates; choose one with storyline.pick.

tools.name: film.get_look
tools.description: Get the project's film look (style, grade, film stock, camera body, default models)

tools.name: film.update_look
tools.description: Set the project's film look (§36). Fields merge into the current look unless replace is true. Set this first: every shot prompt inherits it.

tools.name: generation.list_models
tools.description: List the generation models (image and video) with their capabilities and prices in milli-credits (1000 = 1 credit).

tools.name: character.list
tools.description: List the project's cast with each character's reference images (the character map)

tools.name: character.get
tools.description: Get one character and its reference images

tools.name: character.create
tools.description: Add a recurring character to the cast. Describe appearance precisely — it drives the generated reference sheet.

tools.name: character.update
tools.description: Update a character's name, description or voice

tools.name: character.set_primary
tools.description: Choose which reference image anchors the character's identity in generated views and shots

tools.name: character.delete
tools.description: Remove a character (and its reference sheet) from the cast

tools.name: character.add_reference
tools.description: Attach an image asset (e.g. an uploaded photo via asset.upload) to a character as one view of its character map. The first reference becomes the identity anchor.

tools.name: character.remove_reference
tools.description: Remove one reference image from a character's map

tools.name: character.generate_sheet
tools.description: Generate the character map (front, ¾ left/right, profile, back, full body, close-up) with an image model, keeping one identity. With no reference yet, a front portrait is generated first from the description. Costs credits per image (see generation.list_models), charged to the project owner. Runs in

tools.name: character.generate_view
tools.description: Generate (or regenerate) one view of a character's map, e.g. an expression. Costs credits, charged to the project owner.

tools.name: location.list
tools.description: List the project's location library with each location's reference plates

tools.name: location.get
tools.description: Get one location and its reference plates

tools.name: location.create
tools.description: Add a recurring location (setting) to the library. Describe it precisely — it drives the generated plates. Assign it to scenes with scene.update locationId; shots inherit it.

tools.name: location.update
tools.description: Update a location's name or description

tools.name: location.delete
tools.description: Remove a location (and its plates) from the library. Scenes and shots set there fall back to text only.

tools.name: location.add_reference
tools.description: Attach an image asset (e.g. an uploaded photo via asset.upload) to a location as one of its reference plates (wide, reverse, detail or custom)

tools.name: location.remove_reference
tools.description: Remove one reference plate from a location

tools.name: location.generate_plates
tools.description: Generate a location's reference plates (wide, reverse angle, detail) with an image model, keeping one place. With no plate yet, the first is drawn from the description. Costs credits per image (see generation.list_models), charged to the project owner. Runs in the background — poll generation.list.

tools.name: shot.list
tools.description: List shots (with camera settings) for one scene, or for the whole project

tools.name: shot.get
tools.description: Get one shot

tools.name: shot.create
tools.description: Add a shot to a scene with camera direction (§38). Each shot gets its own video clip on the timeline; the scene's length becomes the sum of its shots and later clips ripple. The first shot of a scene takes over the scene's existing video placeholder.

tools.name: shot.update
tools.description: Change a shot's story, cast, framing, camera rig, lighting, reference videos or duration (a duration change ripples later clips)

tools.name: shot.delete
tools.description: Delete a shot; later clips close up. Deleting a scene's last shot keeps its clip as the scene's picture slot.

tools.name: shot.reorder
tools.description: Move a shot to a new position within its scene (its clips are re-laid out in the new order)

tools.name: shot.compile_prompt
tools.description: Preview exactly what would be sent to the generation model for a shot — compiled prompt, reference images and videos, duration and cost. ignoredReferenceVideos counts the shot's reference videos the model won't receive; referenceVideoMode is follow or edit; problem says why shot.generate_video would

tools.name: shot.generate_keyframe
tools.description: Generate keyframe image variants for a shot from its camera direction, cast references and location plates. The first variant becomes the start frame if the shot has none. Costs credits per image, charged to the project owner. Runs in the background — poll generation.list.

tools.name: shot.select_keyframe
tools.description: Use an image asset (usually a keyframe variant) as the shot's start or end frame

tools.name: shot.generate_video
tools.description: Generate a video take for a shot using its camera movement, action and cast. An image_to_video model animates the start frame (shot.generate_keyframe first); a reference_to_video model needs no start frame and follows the shot's reference videos (shot.update referenceVideoAssetIds), using the keyfra

tools.name: shot.select_take
tools.description: Put a generated take (video asset) on the shot's timeline clip

tools.name: shot.add_still
tools.description: Add an existing image asset (e.g. a frame from asset.capture_frame, or an upload) to a shot's stills, free of charge. asStartFrame makes it the frame the video animates from; a shot without a start frame always gets it.

tools.name: shot.remove_keyframe
tools.description: Remove a generated still (keyframe asset) from a shot. If it was the shot's start or end frame, that frame is cleared. Undoable; credits are not refunded.

tools.name: music.compile_prompt
tools.description: Preview what music.generate would send to Lyria for a placeholder — prompt, length, model and cost. Free.

tools.name: music.generate
tools.description: Generate a music track with Google Lyria (the model behind Flow Music) for a music/ambience placeholder, sized to the clip. Costs credits per track, charged to the project owner. Runs in the background — poll generation.list with placeholderId. The finished track fills the clip (undoable).

tools.name: voice.list
tools.description: List the ElevenLabs voices characters and voice clips can speak with (id, name, labels like gender/accent, a preview URL). Free.

tools.name: voice.compile
tools.description: Preview what voice.generate would speak for a voice placeholder — text, voice, model and cost. Free.

tools.name: voice.generate
tools.description: Speak a line with ElevenLabs for a voice placeholder (narration, off-screen dialogue — no lip-sync). Costs credits per character, charged to the project owner. Runs in the background — poll generation.list with placeholderId. The finished audio fills the clip (undoable).

tools.name: shot.lipsync
tools.description: Give a shot's take spoken dialogue with matching lips: ElevenLabs speaks the line in the speaker's voice (character.update voiceId), then a lip-sync model reworks the take's mouth to it. Works with any video model; best on close and medium shots with one visible face. The result is a new take with t

tools.name: shot.revoice
tools.description: Re-voice a take that has native speech (made with generateAudio on a model like Seedance 2.5, Kling O3 or Wan 3): ElevenLabs' voice changer converts the speech to the speaker's voice and keeps its timing, so the lips still match. One voice for the whole track — for single-speaker shots; ambience in

tools.name: generation.list
tools.description: List generation jobs (character views, location plates, keyframes, takes, lip-synced/re-voiced takes, music, voice lines) for a project, newest first, optionally for one shot, character, location or music/voice placeholder. outputAssetIds are the results.

tools.name: generation.status
tools.description: Get one generation job's status, progress and outputs

tools.name: generation.cancel
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running generation. A job that hasn't reached the provider is refunded.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: voice.list · Private data: project.export, project.import, asset.get, prompt.attach, prompt.get, credits.list_history, render.get_result, render.delete, asset.upload · Public sink: track.reorder, asset.upload, character.add_reference, location.add_reference, shot.add_still, music.compile_prompt · Destructive: project.delete, track.delete, scene.delete, timeline.delete_item, timeline.batch, timeline.add_transitions, timeline.remove_transitions, timeline.remove_transition, scenario.delete, render.delete, character.delete, character.remove_reference, location.delete, location.remove_reference, shot.delete, shot.remove_keyframe.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: voice.list · Private data: project.export, project.import, asset.get, prompt.attach, prompt.get, credits.list_history, render.get_result, render.delete, asset.upload · Public sink: track.reorder, asset.upload, character.add_reference, location.add_reference, shot.add_still, music.compile_prompt · Destructive: project.delete, track.delete, scene.delete, timeline.delete_item, timeline.batch, timeline.add_transitions, timeline.remove_transitions, timeline.remove_transition, scenario.delete, render.delete, character.delete, character.remove_reference, location.delete, location.remove_reference, shot.delete, shot.remove_keyframe

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
